title: Local complete-intersection deformations with a Fitting-ideal bound
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $A$ be a complete-intersection local $k$-algebra [def-trf-complete-intersection-local-algebra]. Write $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m_A$ for its residue field and set $d=\dim A+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa$, where $\dim A$ is ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and transcendence degree is [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Put $R=k[[t]]$, the formal power-series ring. There are an integer $e\geq0$ and a local $R$-algebra $B$, flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and essentially of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], together with a $k$-algebra isomorphism $B/tB\cong A$, such that $t^e\in\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega_{B/R})$. Here $\Omega_{B/R}$ is the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $\operatorname{Fit}_d$ is the presentation-independent kernel-minor ideal of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0E7X, lemma-smoothing-at-lci-point; the final construction B = Q_q makes B local.

proof.text: By [def-trf-complete-intersection-local-algebra] and [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], write $A=W^{-1}S$ for a finite type $k$-algebra $S$ and a multiplicative subset $W$. Let $\mathfrak p_0$ be the inverse image in $S$ of the maximal ideal of $A$. Every $w\in W$ maps to a unit, so $W\cap\mathfrak p_0=\varnothing$. Every $s\notin\mathfrak p_0$ also maps to a unit, since $A$ is local. Thus the maps $W^{-1}S\to S_{\mathfrak p_0}$ and $S_{\mathfrak p_0}\to A$, given respectively by $s/w\mapsto s/w$ and $s/u\mapsto(s/1)(u/1)^{-1}$, are inverse $k$-algebra maps, as is checked on fractions. Hence $A\cong S_{\mathfrak p_0}$.

source.place: 0E7X, first sentence: expressing the essentially finite type local algebra as a prime localization, expanded on fractions

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-ci-local-ring-principal-neighbourhood] to $S$ and $\mathfrak p_0$: its complete-intersection local-ring hypothesis is precisely the hypothesis on $A\cong S_{\mathfrak p_0}$. Obtain $h\notin\mathfrak p_0$ such that $P=S_h$ is a global complete intersection. With $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_0S_h$ we have $P_{\mathfrak p}\cong S_{\mathfrak p_0}\cong A$: both localizations invert exactly the elements needed to invert every element of $S\setminus\mathfrak p_0$, and the inverse maps send each fraction to the same fraction. In particular $P\neq0$.

source.place: 0E7X, first sentence, via the existing principal-neighbourhood form of the global complete-intersection localization theorem

proof.text: Choose a global complete-intersection presentation $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ with $\dim P=N-c$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. By [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-equidimensional], $\dim_{\mathfrak p}\operatorname{Spec}P=N-c$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] to this finite type $k$-algebra and prime: its right side is $\dim P_{\mathfrak p}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\dim A+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa=d$, because the local $k$-algebra isomorphism identifies maximal ideals and residue fields. Thus $d=N-c=\dim P\geq0$.

source.place: 0E7X, second sentence, dimension computation including the equidimensionality needed to replace dimension at the prime by global dimension

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-global-ci-smoothing] to the presentation of $P$ in Step 3, with $r=d$. It gives $Q=R[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$, flat over $R=k[[t]]$, an isomorphism $Q/tQ\cong P$, a smooth generic-fibre morphism $\operatorname{Spec}Q[1/t]\to\operatorname{Spec}k((t))$, and pure dimension $d$ for every nonempty geometric fibre. Its displayed presentation makes $Q$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra].

source.place: 0E7X, third sentence and the following assertion about the relative dimension of the constructed Q

proof.text: The $Q$-module $M=\Omega_{Q/R}$ is generated by $\mathrm dx_1,\ldots,\mathrm dx_N$. Indeed every element of $Q$ is represented by a polynomial in the $x_i$ over $R$; additivity, the Leibniz rule and vanishing on $R$ give $\mathrm dF=\sum_i (\partial F/\partial x_i)\,\mathrm dx_i$. The symbols $\mathrm dq$ generate $\Omega_{Q/R}$ in its construction [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], so these finitely many differentials suffice. Consequently $I=\operatorname{Fit}_d(M)\subset Q$ is defined by [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change].

source.place: 0E7X, introduction of the dth Fitting ideal; finite generation expanded from the universal differential construction

proof.text: Let $f:\operatorname{Spec}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. It is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], and locally of finite presentation by the displayed presentation and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Its nonempty geometric fibres have pure dimension $d$ by Step 4. The relative differential sheaf is the sheaf associated to $M$ by [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Hence [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus] applies and identifies $V(I)$ with the nonsmooth locus of $f$. Step 4 gives smoothness of the restriction $D(t)\to\operatorname{Spec}R[1/t]$. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] makes $D(t)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ smooth as well. Thus $V(I)\cap D(t)=\varnothing$, or $V(I)\subseteq V(t)$.

source.place: 0E7X, application of the Fitting-ideal smooth-locus criterion and smoothness away from t

proof.text: Every prime ideal of $Q$ containing $I$ contains $t$ by Step 6. By the intersection-of-primes formula in [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], $t\in\sqrt I$. The same cited statement defines $\sqrt I$ by positive powers, so there is $e\geq1$ with $t^e\in I$. This supplies the required nonnegative exponent; if $I=Q$ one could also take $e=0$.

source.place: 0E7X, sentence Thus t^n is in I for some n, expanded through the radical formula

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset Q$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak p\subset P$ under $Q\to Q/tQ\cong P$, and set $B=Q_{\mathfrak q}$. This is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. It is flat over $R$ by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness], applied to the flat $R$-module $Q$ and the multiplicative set $Q\setminus\mathfrak q$. Since $Q$ is finite type over $R$, $B$ is essentially finite type by [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] to the ideal $tQ$ gives $B/tB\cong(Q/tQ)_{\mathfrak p}\cong P_{\mathfrak p}\cong A$. These maps are $k$-linear: the quotient/localization map sends the class of $q/s$ to $\bar q/\bar s$ and fixes $k$.

source.place: 0E7X, final two sentences: q is the inverse image of p and B is Q_q

proof.text: Put $U=Q\setminus\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], $\Omega_{B/R}\cong U^{-1}M$. The canonical tensor/fraction identification $M\otimes_QB\cong U^{-1}M$ sends $m\otimes(q/s)$ to $qm/s$ and has inverse $m/s\mapsto m\otimes(1/s)$. Balancing defines the forward map. If $m/s=m\prime/s\prime$, choose $u\in U$ with $u(s\prime m-sm\prime)=0$; the difference of the proposed inverse images is $u(s\prime m-sm\prime)\otimes1/(uss\prime)=0$. The inverse is additive and balanced by the same common-denominator calculation. The two composites fix pure tensors and fractions. Thus $\Omega_{B/R}\cong M\otimes_QB$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] to the ring map $Q\to B$ and the finite generating surjection $Q^{\oplus N}\to M$ from Step 5. It gives $\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega_{B/R})=IB$. Here the isomorphism does not alter the Fitting ideal: composing a free surjection with a module isomorphism leaves its kernel, and hence every defining kernel minor, unchanged. The image of $t^e\in I$ is therefore in $\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega_{B/R})$, completing every clause.

source.place: 0E7X, concluding localization, using 00RT and Fitting base change to retain the parameter-power bound
